URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/24/houthis-launch-attacks-on-saudi-arabia-and-yemens-aden
Al Jazeera (Al Jazeera Staff and AFP), published 24 Oct 2026, updated with Sunday material. Cross-referenced to the Times of Israel live blog entry at 5:47 AM Israel time = 03:47 GMT Sun 25 Oct 2026 (Israel also moved to UTC+2 on 25 Oct). Compiled 08:48 GMT Sun 25 Oct.

SECOND SOURCE URL: https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog-october-25-2026/

THE OVERNIGHT ADVANCE ON LAST NIGHT'S TAIF/YANBU ITEM — A MISSILE OVER THE CAPITAL
- "The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Sunday that it downed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital, Riyadh."
- Coalition spokesperson, in a social media post: "Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh."
- Times of Israel carries the identical coalition statement at 03:47 GMT: "Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh." TWO APPROVED SOURCES on the central claim.
- Al Jazeera's live blog for 25 Oct is headlined "Iran war live: Saudi downs Houthi ballistic missile targeting Riyadh".

THE AIRPORT REOPENING AND THE HOUTHI THREAT AGAINST IT — THE STRONGEST SUNDAY DETAIL
- "Riyadh's international airport said in a social media post on Saturday that flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following Houthi strikes on the capital."
- "Shortly after the announcement, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree issued a warning on X, saying the airport is still 'unsafe' and remains a 'military target'."
- "The Flightradar24 monitoring site showed a plane taking off from Riyadh airport early on Sunday, heading to the Saudi city of Jeddah." (Flightradar24 is not an approved domain; it is cited inside Al Jazeera's copy, which is the source of record.)
- Earlier context, CBS: one strike on Riyadh's King Khalid Airport earlier this month killed at least a dozen people, including a US citizen, and injured hundreds more.

TARGET CONFLICT FROM SATURDAY (do not average or merge — these are competing claims)
- CNBC, 24 Oct: "The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired by the group, aimed towards Taif and Yanbu." This matches what we published last night.
- Al Jazeera, 24 Oct: "On Saturday, Saudi Arabia's civil defence said on X the Houthis had launched two ballistic missiles towards Mecca and Medina, warning of 'the fall of shrapnel' following their interception." Images shared on X by the Saudi Press Agency appeared to show a large, blackened missile-shaped object that had landed somewhere in Saudi Arabia.
- THE HOUTHIS DENY THE MECCA/MEDINA CLAIM: "The Houthis said the claim that they targeted the two cities - the holiest in Islam - was a 'huge lie'. They said their targets were three Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and an airbase."
- So there are two different Saudi official accounts of Saturday's two missiles (Taif and Yanbu per the coalition via CNBC; Mecca and Medina per civil defence via Al Jazeera) plus a Houthi denial. Report all three or none.

OTHER HARD FACTS
- Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, secretary-general of the Gulf Cooperation Council, described the Houthi attacks as "heinous" and said they embodied "a blatant disregard for the lives and security of civilians", in a statement shared on Saturday.
- Yemen's internationally recognised government's Ministry of Transport, in a Facebook post on Saturday, denounced the Houthis' targeting of Aden international airport with two ballistic missiles, calling it the "fourth such attack this month", warning it poses "a threat to the safety of civil aviation" with "humanitarian and economic repercussions for citizens".
- Yemeni authorities said the coastguard headquarters and a second building were also hit. The Houthis claimed attacks on the al-Nasr camp and Aden's naval military base.
- Houthi-run Al Masirah TV said Saudi-led coalition air attacks killed several civilians in Sanaa and Hodeidah. Al Jazeera states the claim could not be verified and Saudi Arabia has not commented. DO NOT USE AS FACT.
- Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said on Saturday government forces carried out more than 700 "targeting operations" in 24 hours, "neutralising" 300 Houthi fighters. This is one belligerent's own claim, unverified.
- The Houthis have targeted Saudi energy infrastructure and airports with long-range strikes since a fragile ceasefire agreed in 2022 fell apart in July.
- Also on Sunday, per Iran International (facts only): the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile fired by the Houthis toward Khamis Mushait. Single-source, Iran International only — treat as unconfirmed.
